# Rating

> A row of native radios from 1 to `max`, with one label and one value, that previews the value under the pointer.

`<slab-rating>` · Form · built on `[role=radiogroup] + <input type=radio>s`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/rating/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/rating.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-rating label="Rating" name="rating" value="3"></slab-rating>
```

Nothing is drawn, so give each `::part(star)` a look, and `::part(filled)` the look of the value. The radios are named by their numbers and the group by `label`, so a screenreader reads "Rating, 3, radio button, 3 of 5". While the pointer is over a radio, the radios up to it are `filled` instead and the host is `:state(previewing)`, which can tell a preview apart from the value.

To name the radios by what they mean, such as "3 stars", set `formatValue` to a function of each radio's number.

With `step="0.5"`, each star is two radios, named "0.5", "1", "1.5" and so on, and the value can be a half. A star's first radio is also `::part(start)` and its second `::part(end)`, so style each as half of a star, such as by clipping each to its half.

With `readonly`, the value can't be changed but the rating can still be focused, read and submitted, where `disabled` leaves it out of the form. It doesn't preview under the pointer, and the host is `:state(readonly)`.

## Keyboard

| Key                   | What it does                                                       |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Tab                   | Moves into the rating at the checked radio, or the first, and out. |
| Up, Down, Left, Right | Moves to the previous or next radio and checks it.                 |
| Space                 | Checks the focused radio.                                          |
| Enter                 | Submits the form, as on a native radio.                            |

## Elements

### `<slab-rating>`

Import `slab-elements/rating.js` to register it.

A rating with no visual styles: a row of native radios, one for each point from 1 to `max`, with one label, one value, and one validity for all of them. With `step="0.5"`, there's one for each half point instead, two to a star.

The radios are the platform's, in the shadow root, so they're checked, moved between with the arrow keys, and read the way a native radio group is. Each is named by its number, and the group by `label`, so a screenreader reads "Label, 3, radio button, 3 of 5". Set `formatValue` to a function of the number to name each radio by what it means instead, such as "3 stars".

Each radio is a `star` part. Those up to the value are `filled` as well, and while one is hovered, those up to it are `filled` instead, so a pointer previews the value it would pick. The host is `:state(previewing)` while it does. Nothing is drawn, so a star, a heart, or a radio button is yours to decide. With half steps, each star's two radios are its `start` and `end` halves, so a half-filled star is a filled `start` beside an unfilled `end`.

`readonly` shows the value without letting the user change it. Native radios have no `readonly`, so a click, Space and the arrow keys are kept from checking a different radio instead, and the group is `aria-readonly`.

Style it through its parts and through `:state(disabled)`, `:state(error)`, `:state(previewing)`, `:state(readonly)`, and `:state(required)`. How the radios are arranged is layout, so it's left to the styles around them.

#### Attributes

| Name               | Type       | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------ | ---------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` (required) | `string`   |         | Names it. It's the accessible name, and the visible label where there is one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `disabled`         | `boolean`  | `false` | Disables it, as `disabled` does a native control: the user can't focus or use it, and a form control's value isn't submitted.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `hide-label`       | `boolean`  | `false` | Hides the label visually and leaves it as the accessible name, for a design that shows the label some other way.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `max`              | `number`   | `5`     | How many stars there are. Anything but a whole number of 1 or more is 5.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `name`             | `string`   | `''`    | The name its value is submitted under, as a native control's `name`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `readonly`         | `boolean`  | `false` | Shows the value without letting the user change it, for a rating that's only there to be read. It's still focusable and submitted, and never invalid, as a native read-only input isn't.                                                                                                                                   |
| `required`         | `boolean`  | `false` | Makes it invalid while it has no value, as `required` does a native control.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `step`             | `1 \| 0.5` | `1`     | 1 for whole stars, or 0.5 for half stars. Anything else is 1.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `value`            | `string`   | `''`    | The checked radio's number. Like a native input, the attribute is the default value and the property is the current one. A value that isn't one of the radios' numbers, from `step` to `max`, checks nothing and reads back as an empty string.                                                                            |
| `custom-validity`  | `string`   |         | Makes it invalid with this message, as `setCustomValidity()` does, and shows the message at once rather than once validity is reported, for an error the page already knows about, such as one from a server. Removing it, or setting it to an empty string, makes it valid again, unless something else makes it invalid. |

#### Properties

| Name                            | Type                                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `formatValue`                   | `(value: number) => string \| undefined` | Names each radio from its number, such as "3 stars" rather than "3". The number itself when unset.                                                                                         |
| `defaultValue`                  | `string`                                 | The value it starts with, and goes back to when its form resets. It's the `value` attribute, as a native input's `defaultValue` is, so setting it sets the attribute, and `value` with it. |
| `form` (read-only)              | `HTMLFormElement \| null`                | The form it belongs to, or `null`.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `labels` (read-only)            | `NodeList`                               | The `<label>` elements associated with it, as a native control's `labels`: each `<label for>` that names its `id`, and a `<label>` around it.                                              |
| `validationMessage` (read-only) | `string`                                 | What's wrong, as the validity message says it: the message given to `setCustomValidity()` or `setValidity()`, or else the browser's own. Empty while it's valid.                           |
| `validity` (read-only)          | `ValidityState`                          | Its `ValidityState`, as a native control's.                                                                                                                                                |
| `willValidate` (read-only)      | `boolean`                                | Whether its validity is checked when its form submits. It isn't while it's disabled or read-only.                                                                                          |

#### Methods

| Signature                                                         | Description                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checkValidity(): boolean`                                        | Whether its value is valid. Dispatches "invalid" when it isn't, as a native control's does.                                   |
| `focus(options?: FocusOptions): void`                             | Focuses it, or the part of it that takes focus.                                                                               |
| `reportValidity(): boolean`                                       | Whether its value is valid. When it isn't, dispatches "invalid" and shows the validity message, as a native control's does.   |
| `resetValidityFeedback(): void`                                   | Clears the validity feedback without changing `validity`.                                                                     |
| `setCustomValidity(message: string): void`                        | Makes it invalid with a message of your own, or valid again with an empty one, as a native control's does.                    |
| `setValidity(flags?: ValidityStateFlags, message?: string): void` | Sets its validity and message, as `ElementInternals.setValidity()` does, for checks of your own beyond `setCustomValidity()`. |

#### Events

| Name      | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `input`   | `Event` | As the user changes its value, as a native control's does. Setting it from code doesn't dispatch it.                                                                                    |
| `change`  | `Event` | When the user changes its value, as a native control's does. Setting it from code doesn't dispatch it.                                                                                  |
| `invalid` | `Event` | When a check finds its value invalid, as a native control's does. Cancel it to leave the validity message unshown, after a blur, a submit or `reportValidity()`, and focus where it is. |

#### Slots

| Name               | Type                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------ | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `description`      | `Element \| string` | Text that describes it, such as a hint or what the validity message means. It's its accessible description.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `validity-message` | `Element \| string` | Shown in place of the validity message's text while it's invalid and the message shows, for wording of your own, a translation, or a link. It's part of its accessible description, and `validationMessage` stays the browser's or `setCustomValidity()`'s. |

#### CSS parts

| Name               | Description                                                     |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `description`      | Text about the rating, and its validity message when it has one |
| `end`              | With half steps, the radio for the second half of a star        |
| `filled`           | Each radio up to the value, or up to the hovered one            |
| `label`            | The label                                                       |
| `star`             | Each radio                                                      |
| `stars`            | The radios                                                      |
| `start`            | With half steps, the radio for the first half of a star         |
| `validity-message` | The validity message, which says why the value is invalid       |

#### CSS states

| Name                 | Description                                                                                                               |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:state(disabled)`   | While it's disabled.                                                                                                      |
| `:state(error)`      | While it's invalid and its validity message shows, which is once its validity is reported, as when its form is submitted. |
| `:state(previewing)` | While the pointer rests on a rating other than its value, showing what it would change to.                                |
| `:state(readonly)`   | While it's read-only.                                                                                                     |
| `:state(required)`   | While it's required, for styles such as an asterisk.                                                                      |
